topicName: EC2 Auto Scaling (Scaling Policies, Launch Configurations/Templates)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"EC2 Auto Scaling: Scaling Policies and Launch Configurations/Templates"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"EC2 Auto Scaling helps you maintain application availability and allows you to automatically add or remove EC2 instances based on demand. This tutorial covers scaling policies and launch configurations/templates, which are fundamental components of Auto Scaling."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Launch Configurations and Launch Templates"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A launch configuration or launch template specifies the instance configuration. This includes the AMI ID, instance type, key pair, security groups, and block device mappings. Launch templates are the newer, preferred method."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Launch Configurations (Legacy)"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Launch configurations are immutable after creation. If you need to change the configuration, you must create a new launch configuration."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"AMI: The Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to use for the instance."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Instance Type: The type of EC2 instance (e.g., t2.micro, m5.large)."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Security Groups: One or more security groups to associate with the instance."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Key Pair: The key pair to use for SSH access to the instance."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"User Data: Optional script to run when the instance starts."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Launch Templates (Recommended)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Launch templates are versioned, allowing you to make changes and track revisions. They also support specifying a wider range of EC2 features."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Versioning: You can create multiple versions of a launch template."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Partial Configurations: You can specify only the parameters you want to change, inheriting the rest from a previous version or a default template."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Instance Market Options: Support for Spot Instances and On-Demand Instances."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Network Interfaces: More flexible network interface configurations."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Example AWS CLI command to create a launch template
aws ec2 create-launch-template \
    --launch-template-name my-launch-template \
    --launch-template-data file://launch-template-data.json"},{"order":19,"type":"heading","text":"Scaling Policies"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Scaling policies define how the Auto Scaling group adjusts the number of instances. There are several types of scaling policies:"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Target Tracking Scaling"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Target tracking scaling adjusts the number of instances to maintain a specified target value for a metric. For example, you can target 50% CPU utilization."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"# Example AWS CLI command to create a target tracking scaling policy
aws autoscaling put-scaling-policy \
    --policy-name target-tracking-policy \
    --auto-scaling-group-name my-auto-scaling-group \
    --policy-type TargetTrackingScaling \
    --target-tracking-configuration '{"TargetValue":50.0,"PredefinedMetricSpecification":{"PredefinedMetricType":"ASGAverageCPUUtilization"},"ScaleOutCooldown":300,"ScaleInCooldown":300}'"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Step Scaling"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Step scaling adjusts the number of instances based on step adjustments. Each adjustment specifies the number of instances to add or remove based on the magnitude of the alarm breach."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"# Example AWS CLI command to create a step scaling policy
aws autoscaling put-scaling-policy \
    --policy-name step-scaling-policy \
    --auto-scaling-group-name my-auto-scaling-group \
    --policy-type StepScaling \
    --adjustment-type ChangeInCapacity \
    --step-adjustments '{"MetricIntervalLowerBound":0.0,"ScalingAdjustment":1},{"MetricIntervalLowerBound":50.0,"ScalingAdjustment":2}' \
    --metric-aggregation-type Average \
    --cooldown 300"},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Simple Scaling (Legacy)"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Simple scaling adjusts the number of instances by a fixed amount based on a CloudWatch alarm. It's less flexible than step scaling or target tracking scaling."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Predictive Scaling"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Predictive scaling uses machine learning to forecast future traffic and proactively scale the Auto Scaling group. This helps to ensure that you have enough capacity to handle anticipated demand."},{"order":31,"type":"heading","text":"Putting it All Together"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"To use EC2 Auto Scaling effectively, you need to:"},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create a launch template (recommended) or launch configuration."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create an Auto Scaling group, specifying the launch template/configuration, desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Define scaling policies to automatically adjust the number of instances based on demand. Target tracking is often a good starting point."},{"order":36,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor your application and adjust the scaling policies as needed to optimize performance and cost."},{"order":37,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"EC2 Auto Scaling, with its scaling policies and launch configurations/templates, is a powerful tool for managing the capacity of your applications in AWS. By understanding these components, you can build scalable, resilient, and cost-effective systems."}]
